audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL: EL state transitions (DAO fork, Berlin block processing, Cancun gas/precompiles), EL networking (typed transaction gossip via devp2p), CL beacon chain operations (Electra deposits, consolidations, withdrawals, attestations, churn limits), CL stateless validation (EIP-8025 execution proofs), SSZ serialization (EIP-7916 progressive lists), and wallet-level key encapsulation (EIP-6051).

in_scope: State Transition (DAO fork, Berlin block processing)
Gas Economics (blob gas, memory, storage, message call)

out_of_scope: Execution Layer internals from CL perspective

misclassified_entities.reason: SSZ serializer is an internal component of consensus/execution clients, not an external entity. It processes data already within the system boundary.
Generic 'Data Source' for SSZ serialization is an internal component providing list data within the same client process.
ExecutionEngine is a co-located internal component of the node (EL client). While it crosses a process boundary, it is authenticated via JWT and is part of the audited system.
ProofEngine is a co-located internal component for stateless validation. It is part of the node's trusted computing base.
The transport channel is infrastructure, not an entity that sends data. The actual threat actors are the sender/recipient apps and network attackers.
This is a data classification, not an external entity. The actual entity is the calling contract.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer. Can send arbitrary typed transactions, unknown transaction types, or malformed payloads. Consolidates EXT-PEER-NODE and EXT-NETWORK-PEER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated user submitting transactions (including access list txs and blob txs). Consolidates EXT-TX-SENDER and EXT-BLOB-TX-SUBMITTER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner/Validator) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers are not trusted for content correctness. Blocks must be fully validated including PoW (Berlin), extraData (DAO fork), and state roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input data. Gas metering is the primary defense. Consolidates EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT and EXT-CALLER.

trusted_external_entities.name: DAO Token Holder via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: withdraw() function call on WithdrawDAO recovery contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user calling contract function. Balance verification is required before fund transfer.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL communicates with EL over JWT-authenticated Engine API. Channel is authenticated but payload content (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations) must be validated. The EL must verify execution requests from CL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (attestation, beacon block proposal topics)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit attestations and blocks over unauthenticated P2P. Attestation committee_bits, aggregation_bits, and BLS signatures must all be validated. Malicious validators may submit conflicting attestations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL delivers execution-layer requests (deposit requests up to 8192/payload, withdrawal requests up to 16/payload, consolidation requests up to 2/payload) via authenticated Engine API. Content must be validated: BLS signatures on deposits, withdrawal credential matching, consolidation eligibility.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Proof Prover via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Active validators submitting execution proofs. Must verify: prover is active validator, BLS signature valid (DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF 0x0D000000), proof cryptographically valid via ProofEngine. Proof size capped at MAX_PROOF_SIZE (300 KiB).

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client Proof Consumer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Merkle proof requests (EIP-7916 progressive list proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients request merkle proofs for list elements. Requests are unauthenticated. Progressive tree gindex computation must be correct to prevent proof forgery.

trusted_external_entities.name: Key Encapsulation Peer (Sender/Recipient App)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet applications exchanging private keys via ECIES. Recipient public key may lack signature verification (optional signerPubKey). Man-in-the-middle possible without trust chain validation. Consolidates EXT-SENDER-APP, EXT-RECIPIENT-APP, EXT-KEY-PROVIDER, EXT-KEY-HOLDER.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Must validate transaction type byte (0-0x7f range), reject unknown types with peer disconnect (SHOULD), validate payload per type-specific rules. Must not process transactions for types not yet activated by fork block.

Full block validation required: header validation (gas, difficulty, PoW), ommer validation (max 2, age 1-6), transaction list validation (all types known and valid), state/receipt/tx root verification. Reject blocks with unknown transaction types.

Full transaction validation: signature recovery, nonce match, balance >= gas*price + value, sender is EOA, gas available in block. For access list txs: validate access list entries. For blob txs: validate blob gas pricing (GAS_PER_BLOB * count * blob_base_fee).

PoW validation (Ethash, mix digest, difficulty target), extraData validation during DAO fork range (blocks 1920000-1920009 must contain 'dao-hard-fork'), difficulty calculation with bomb delay. All state roots must be recomputed and verified.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: CALL to precompile addresses (0x02 SHA256, 0x04 Identity)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Gas metering must accurately reflect computation cost. Identity: base + per-word. SHA256: base + per-word. Arbitrary input size bounded only by gas. No content validation needed (precompiles are pure functions).
Must verify caller's DAO token balance via mainDAO contract before transferring proportional ether. Transfer failure must throw exception.

JWT authentication verified. Execution payload content must still be validated: state transition correctness, gas accounting, transaction execution. EIP-8025 dual validation requires both ExecutionEngine and ProofEngine agreement.

Must validate committee_bits (within MAX_COMMITTEES_PER_SLOT), compute attesting indices from aggregation_bits, verify aggregate BLS signature. Detect conflicting attestations for slashing (penalty: effective_balance / 4096).

Validate BLS deposit signature (is_valid_deposit_signature). Queue as PendingDeposit. Process at epoch boundary respecting: finality check (deposit slot must be finalized), MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH (16), activation churn limits. EL enforces MAX_DEPOSIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD (8192).

Validate source_address matches 0x01 withdrawal credentials, validator is active and not exiting. Amount=0 means full exit (compute exit epoch with churn). Non-zero amount queues PendingPartialWithdrawal. Max 16 per payload. Sweep max 8 per block.

Validate source_address matches withdrawal credentials, both validators active, source != target, neither slashed. Same-validator triggers compounding switch (0x01 -> 0x02). Cross-validator queues PendingConsolidation. Max 2 per payload.

Three-stage validation: (1) prover_pubkey belongs to active validator, (2) BLS signature valid under DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, (3) proof cryptographically valid via proof_engine.verify_execution_proof. Reject at any failure stage. Max proof size 300 KiB.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Merkle proof API (EIP-7916 progressive list proofs)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Proof generation must use stable generalized indices that are capacity-independent. Progressive tree structure must provide equivalent security to fixed-capacity merkle trees. Context-specific bounds enforcement required.

Recipient public key should be verified via signerPubKey signature and optional trustedPubKey chain. Ephemeral keys must use CSRNG. ECDH shared secret derived correctly. AES-GCM encryption with HKDF-derived key/IV. Ephemeral keys must be securely destroyed after protocol completion for PFS.
